title: Toward an Integrated IPOO–DMAIC Framework for Diagnosing and Improving Waqf Governance: A Conceptual Case Study Protocol for West Sumatra, Indonesia
journal: Perspectives on Advanced New Generations of Global and Local Economic Horizons
abstract: This paper develops an integrated Input-Process-Output-Outcome (IPOO) and Lean Six Sigma DMAIC framework for diagnosing and improving waqf governance in West Sumatra, Indonesia, and reports its Define-phase output: identifying quick wins, specifying a baseline data-collection plan, proposing tentative root causes for empirical testing, and outlining improvement and control mechanisms. The framework was built through analysis of national and provincial regulations and institutional reports (SIWAK, the Indonesian Waqf Board, the Ministry of Religious Affairs) and a structured synthesis of the waqf-governance and Lean Six Sigma literature, benchmarked against Malaysia, Türkiye, Kuwait, Egypt, and Singapore. A forthcoming empirical phase will use semi-structured interviews, observation, and document analysis, validated through triangulation. Cash waqf collection rose from IDR 763.32 million (2024) to IDR 1.68 billion (April 2026), and the National Waqf Index from 0.422 (2023) to 0.447 (2024). Yet only 3,604 of 5,235 land parcels were certified, leaving 1,631 (31.16%) uncertified. Weak coordination and fragmented data were flagged as priority quick wins, while inadequate nazhir guidance and weak process standardisation emerged as tentative root causes. The Improve phase proposes standardised training, a Waqf Plan of Action, and a monitoring dashboard, with performance indicators specified in the Control phase. Once validated, this framework offers measurable stages for institutionalising continuous improvement in waqf governance.

title: The Impact of Social Media Use on the Communication Behavior of Housewives in Jorong Tanjung Durian, Sangir Jujuan District, South Solok Regency
abstract: Social media is reshaping everyday communication, yet limited attention has been given to how the use of multiple platforms relates to communication behavior among housewives in rural communities. This study examines these relationships in Jorong Tanjung Durian, Sangir Jujuan District, South Solok Regency. A descriptive qualitative approach was employed, involving 18 informants selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through non-participant observation, unstructured in-depth interviews, and document review. Analysis followed the stages of data collection, reduction, display, and conclusion drawing. The findings indicate that WhatsApp, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram facilitated long-distance communication, expanded social relationships, and improved access to everyday information. Less regulated use was associated with reduced attention during face-to-face interactions, lower responsiveness to people nearby, and repetitive engagement that affected time management. These findings suggest that social media supports more flexible communication practices while presenting challenges for balancing digital engagement with direct interpersonal interaction. The study contributes to understanding social action in digital communication within a rural setting and highlights the practical importance of digital literacy that supports attentive interaction, effective time management, and meaningful family and community relationships.

title: TOPOLOGICAL DYNAMICS FOR OPERATORS GENERATED BY GROUP ACTIONS
abstract: In this note, we characterize topologically multiple recurrence for weighted translation operators and a sequence of operators, generated by group actions. Some sufficient conditions for sequences of operators to be disjoint topologically transitive and disjoint topologically mixing are provided as well.

title: PREVALENCE OF BURNOUT AMONG CLINICAL OPTOMETRY STUDENTS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF BENIN, BENIN CITY, EDO STATE.
journal: African Journal of Health, Safety and Environment
abstract: Clinical optometry training requires students to combine academic learning with patient care, clinical assessment and professional competence development. These demands may contribute to burnout-related experiences. This study assessed burnout among clinical optometry students at the University of Benin and examined the association between clinical supervision and burnout. A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 150 clinical optometry students in 500 and 600 levels at the University of Benin. Participants were chosen using proportionate allocation and random sampling. Data were collected with a structured, self-administered questionnaire incorporating an adapted Maslach Burnout Inventory framework assessing emotional exhaustion, depersonalization and personal accomplishments, together with clinical supervision items. Data were analysed using IBM SPSS Statistics version 25.0. Frequencies, percentages and descriptive statistics were used, while Pearson chi-square tests assessed associations at a 5% significance level. Moderate emotional exhaustion was predominant in 78 (52.0%) respondents, depersonalization as low in 92 (61.3%) and personal accomplishment was high in 95 (63.3%). Gender and age were not significantly associated with burnout (p>0.05). Clinical supervision was significantly associated with emotional exhaustion (p=0.004), but not with depersonalization (p=0.130) and personal accomplishment (p=0.113). Clinical optometry students demonstrated a mixed burnout profile characterised by predominantly moderate emotional exhaustion, low depersonalization and high personal accomplishment. The significant relationship between clinical supervision and emotional exhaustion highlights the relevance of the clinical learning environment to students' wellbeing. Strengthening supportive supervision, monitoring workload and improving student support may be useful institutional measures.

title: ‘Breaking cycles’: exploring how women choose childfreedom amid constraints in Türkiye
Urinary Stone Recurrence After Initiation of GLP-1-Based Therapy: A Romanian Retrospective Cohort Study of Clinical, Renal, and Hydration-Related Factors
abstract: Background: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonists produce substantial weight loss and improve glycemic control, but their relationship with urinary stone recurrence remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated clinically and radiologically confirmed recurrent stone episodes occurring after initiation of semaglutide or tirzepatide. Methods: This retrospective single-center cohort screened 168 adults receiving semaglutide or tirzepatide. Four patients with previous bariatric surgery, 33 without at least 6 months of post-initiation clinical follow-up, and five with hyperparathyroidism were excluded, leaving 126 participants. Follow-up was calculated from GLP-1-based therapy initiation to the last documented clinical or imaging assessment. Recurrence required a stone episode documented before treatment initiation and a new symptomatic or radiologically progressive stone event after initiation. Results: The cohort included 94 semaglutide and 32 tirzepatide users. Median follow-up was 9 months [IQR 8–12]. Thirteen patients (10.3%; 95% CI 6.1–16.9%) had a recurrent episode after treatment initiation. No measured demographic, metabolic, renal, hydration-related, electrolyte, or treatment characteristic clearly differentiated patients with and without recurrence. Allopurinol use was more frequent among recurrent stone formers in an unadjusted analysis, a finding considered exploratory and likely affected by confounding by indication. Conclusions: In this single-arm cohort, 10.3% of patients had clinically and radiologically documented stone recurrence after GLP-1-based therapy initiation. The study describes post-initiation events but cannot estimate treatment-attributable risk because it lacked an untreated comparator, pre-treatment incidence-rate analysis, standardized surveillance, and complete exposure data. Larger prospective comparator studies with baseline imaging, time-to-event follow-up, complete urinary chemistry, and treatment-dose data are required.

title: The Impact of Digital Marketing and Delivery Speed on Customer Satisfaction at JNE Express
abstract: Digital transformation and the increasing demand for faster services have made customer satisfaction in courier services dependent not only on the quality of digital interactions but also on delivery performance. This study aims to analyze the effects of digital marketing and delivery speed on customer satisfaction among JNE Express customers. A quantitative approach was employed through a survey of 130 JNE Express customers selected using purposive sampling. Data were collected using a five-point Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results show that digital marketing has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction. Delivery speed also has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction. Simultaneously, both variables have a significant effect on customer satisfaction and explain more than half of the variation in customer satisfaction. These findings indicate that customer experience in courier services is shaped by a combination of relevant digital communication and the company's ability to fulfill service promises quickly and on time. Practically, companies need to integrate digital channel management with improvements in distribution process reliability to provide a more consistent customer experience.
